title: Influence of the Camera Viewing Angle on OpenPose Validity in Motion Analysis
metricDefinition: OpenPose joint angles from multiple viewing directions are compared with marker-based motion capture to quantify view-dependent validity.

extractionLocations.description: Agreement by joint and viewing angle.
View-dependent bias and shoulder-joint validity limitations.

study.deviceAndEnvironment: Four camera views and laboratory marker-based reference

measurements.definition: Agreement and bias of OpenPose-derived knee, hip, elbow, and shoulder joint angles against reference motion capture.
measurements.calculationMethod: Joint-angle comparison across camera viewing directions.
notes: A shoulder joint angle is not a left-right shoulder-line tilt metric.

reportedFindings.summary: Camera viewing direction materially affects markerless joint-angle validity and the shoulder result requires particular caution.

faceFitMappings.reason: The shared angular unit does not make a shoulder joint angle equivalent to a left-right shoulder-line tilt.

thresholdAssessment.reason: View-dependent validity results are algorithm limitations, not behavior boundaries.

limitations: Dynamic laboratory tasks and multiple viewing directions differ from a seated webcam interview.
Shoulder joint-angle semantics must not be substituted for shoulder-line tilt.
